newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zhejiang Expressway ends debut firmer.
newsitem.headline: Zhejiang Expressway ends debut firmer.

text.p: Shares of Zhejiang Expressway Co Ltd ended their first trading day at a disappointing HK$2.50 per share, up slightly from their issue price of HK$2.38 each, analysts said on Thursday.

"It is a little bit disappointed since we expected between 10 and 20 percent growth today," an analyst at a local brokerage house said. Earlier this week, the grey market price for shares of the China toll road operator was about HK$3.50 each.
The stock, which is the second most active counter, moved in a narrow range of between HK$2.40 and HK$2.90 all day on volume of 386.37 million shares worth HK$1.03 billion.
"The company probably has no more new projects in the pipe line in short term other than what it has announced," the analyst at the local house said.
Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities, said the price earnings (P/E) multiple of Zhejiang Expressway looked a bit high.

"Beijing North Star Co Ltd has a much lower P/E," he said. Shares of the China property concern jumped 95 percent from their issue price to close their first trading day on Wednesday at HK$4.672 each.
But they eased HK$0.525 to HK$4.15 on Thursday.
Zhejiang Expressway issued 1.25 billion H-shares to Hong Kong and U.S. and international investors. Its initial public offering of 124.68 million H-shares in Hong Kong was 118 times subscribed.

Analysts also said the toll road operator was a defensive buy because as an infrastructure play it was less sensitive to the overall economic changes and in return it would benefit from the booming economy growth in Shanghai. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6369
